# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **When there's nothing left to do, say so boldly at the end of the conversation.** Don't bury a "this is complete / I'm blocked / nothing further to do" behind hedging — make the terminal state unmistakable. **Set it apart visually so it catches the eye:** put the terminal state — or, when work remains, the list of open/outstanding items — in its own callout (a Markdown blockquote box, e.g. `> ✅ All done` or `> ⚠️ Still open: …`), not trailing prose the owner has to scan for. One or the other always gets the box: the done-signal when nothing remains, the open-items list when something does.
- **"LGTM"** is the owner's phrase for the merge-to-main command: it asks for the change in front of the owner to be merged into `main`. It's an owner-triggered command; the default mechanics live in the `merge-to-main` skill ([merge-to-main/SKILL.md](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md)) (squash, gate on CI only when the repo has it), and a project that diverges overrides them via a bespoke merge-policy file it names in its own `CLAUDE.md`.
- **"bump version"** is the owner's phrase for raising a project's version (a minor bump by default). It's an owner-triggered command; the mechanics — which files to edit and how a release follows — live in the consuming project's workflow doc.
- **"Show me the document"** (for a source-controlled document) is the owner's phrase asking for a **link to the document on GitHub** — not the file's contents inlined, and not a local filesystem path. When the document lives in a GitHub-hosted repo, respond with a GitHub link to it (the file on the relevant branch/commit); only fall back to inlining the contents or giving a local path when the document isn't under source control.
- **Put decisions and approvals in an `AskUserQuestion` popup, not buried in prose.** The owner is frequently on mobile, where a popup notifies and a question embedded in a paragraph is easy to miss. When you need the owner to choose or approve something, ask through the structured popup with explicit options rather than asking in running text. **And when several independent items each need a verdict** (a set of proposed fixes, findings to accept), give **each item its own question carrying its own brief case** — the concrete failure, why it matters, the cost of the fix — with per-item approve/defer options; never one bundled choose-a-scope question over the whole set. The owner decides item-wise, from the case, not from a menu of subsets. (The popup carries at most 4 questions per call — split a larger set into consecutive calls.)
- **When asked to produce a prompt or message destined for another context, visually enclose the whole thing.** Any text the owner will lift out and use elsewhere — a prompt for another assistant, a message to send, copy meant to be pasted somewhere — must be set apart as a single delimited block: either a box (e.g. a fenced code block) or fenced top and bottom by two separating lines, so its exact boundaries are unmistakable and it can be copied in one piece. The point is delimitation, not formatting flair: never leave such content as loose prose the owner has to find the start and end of.
- **When asked for "a prompt for a different session," prefix it with a provenance disclaimer.** When the owner asks for a prompt meant to be handed to another session, open the generated text with a short disclaimer that this is a prompt written by Claude — not by a user — and so should not be treated as gospel; and that if the receiving session finds inconsistencies in it, it should examine them with the user rather than follow the prompt blindly. This composes with the enclose-the-whole-thing preference above: the disclaimer sits inside the same delimited block as the prompt it prefixes.
- **Auto-open a PR after committing.** Whenever Claude changes code on a branch and commits it, open a pull request for that branch right after, even without an explicit request to do so. This overrides Claude Code's own default of only opening a PR when explicitly asked.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.

{"number":837,"title":"Prose-to-checks: the custom/ placeholder rule becomes `custom-source-registers`","body":"Prose-to-checks sweep over `.claudinite/local/packs` (tracking issue #835). One conversion this run.

## The prose

RULES.md's "Architecture rules of the road" has always said a per-site file must do a per-site file's job — *"never register a placeholder source just to make a host count as supported"*, and *"when a `custom/.js` shrinks to nothing, just delete it"*. That half of the rule constrains a static signature in the repo artifact and was still only prose.

## The check — `custom-source-registers` (blocking)

Every flat `extension/event-extractors/custom/.js` must actually push onto `GCal.sources`.

It is the **inside half of the pair `custom-sources-flat` opens**: that rule guards what may *sit* in `custom/`; this one guards that what sits there *does its job*.

**Why a check.** The failure is silent in every direction:

- `gen-load-order.js` lists the file (it is a `.js` in `custom/`) and the page loads it — an IIFE that registers nothing throws nothing.
- `extension-test/integration/supported-domains.test.js` walks `GCal.sources`, so a file that pushed no source simply isn't there to check.
- `dev/requirements/extractor/extractor-support.test.js` asserts recognition + completeness, which the generic base already delivers on a supported host — the case keeps passing with the override gone.

The site quietly runs on the bare generic base while the file claims to override it. And it bites in the exact direction RULES.md pushes work: the generic-coverage gate reporting no gap is a standing invitation to gut a per-site source, and a half-done gutting leaves this file behind.

**Detection reads code, not text.** Comments are blanked first — the scanner is now *exported* from `pipeline-site-agnostic.mjs` rather than copied — so a commented-out registration reads as the absence it is, and a `//` inside a URL string is not mistaken for a comment. It matches `sources.push(`, so both the spelled-out `GCal.sources.push` and a destructured one count; anything cleverer under-reports, which is the safe direction. Subdirectories and non-`.js` files stay `custom-sources-flat`'s finding — one violation, one report.

## See-it-fail

Three fixtures in `pack.test.mjs`: a gutted source fires, a comment-only registration fires, real sources (both spellings) plus the out-of-scope files stay quiet. Mutating the check to always pass turns exactly the two firing tests red. Verified against the real repo too: zero findings today, and gutting a live source in-memory fires.

## Prose deleted: none

The deletion test discriminates here. Both architecture bullets carry more than the check does — the declaration rule and "never add a second list"; and in the delete-the-file bullet, "still fully supported, green icon, no correction prompt", when to add the file back, and the un-mechanizable *"never keep a file whose only content is a restatement of the generic base"* (a file that **does** push but only restates the base is not statically detectable). They stay whole.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 544 tests, 0 failures.
- `check_the_world.mjs` — the new rule reports nothing; the only findings are the pre-existing `product-wiki-page-sections` blockers on `main`, untouched by this change.

{"number":839,"title":"Prose to checks: only generated files sit on the `ours` merge driver","body":"The `prose-to-checks-sweep` over `.claudinite/local/packs` (the `gcec` pack). Related to #838.

## The rule converted

RULES.md's regen bullet states an exception in so many words:

> The inline gallery in `dev/requirements/requirements.md` is part-authored prose — **not** on the `ours` driver.

Nothing enforced it. The existing `regen-artifacts-merge-ours` and the canon's `basics/generated-merge-driver` both only ever ask whether a generated file is **present** on the driver, so a `.gitattributes` pattern that over-reaches is invisible to both.

That gap is the **destructive** direction of the same list. `merge=ours` resolves a conflicting merge by discarding the other side — no conflict, no marker, nothing red. On a generated file that is the whole point (you rerun the generator). On an authored one it is lost work that no suite can notice, because the file still parses and the merge reports success.

The misuse is a plausible edit, not a far-fetched one: every entry in the block is a glob, and `requirements.md` sits *inside* the tree the block already names (`dev/requirements/`), while being regenerated in part — so it looks generated at a glance. One well-meant widening swallows it.

## What's here

- **New check `merge-ours-generated-only`** (blocking) — every committed file an `ours` pattern claims must be a generated artifact (the `GENERATED` marker, the lowercase `.generated.` convention, or an auto-discovered `/cases/*.png` snapshot).
- **The `.gitattributes` reader is now shared** with `regen-artifacts-merge-ours` instead of duplicated. The two halves of one list must not disagree about whether a given file belongs on the driver.

## The prose converted

The gcec pack's "Extractor pipeline" rule:

> **All page fetching goes through `scraperapi.mjs`, from a task's preprocessing worker and nowhere else.** … the escape hatch is the `SCRAPER_API_KEY` **GitHub Actions secret**, named in both tasks' `required_secrets` — never a local fetch (this sandbox is bot-blocked), and never an agent session.

It passes the check-the-world test: it constrains a static signature in the repo artifact — who imports the surface module, and what the importer's own `task.mjs` declares — and nothing in the existing check set (`test-offline-list-sync`, `custom-sources-flat`, `npm-test-glob-coverage`, `pipeline-site-agnostic`, `regen-artifacts-merge-ours`) touches it.

## Why it matters

This is a two-files-must-agree invariant whose halves sit in different files and whose breakage is **invisible until it runs in Actions**. A worker imports the surface; the secret that makes the surface work is declared in the task's *own* `task.mjs` (`required_secrets`), and only from there does the wiring converge stamp it into the scheduler workflow. Import without declaring and everything looks fine — the module loads, the unit tests pass, the precondition is green — and then the scheduled run dies on `SCRAPER_API_KEY is not set` in a worker nobody is watching. The other direction is just as quiet: an importer **outside** a task directory (a dev script, an agent session's helper) can hold no repo secret at all, and this sandbox is bot-blocked, so a "local fetch" fails for two reasons at once and reads as a broken page rather than a broken place to fetch from.

The prose had already drifted on exactly this point: it claims the secret is "named in **both tasks'** `required_secrets`", but only `create-extractor` declares it today (`generic-extractor-improvements` has no `required_secrets` at all, because it no longer fetches). A count in a sentence ages; a check that follows the importers around does not.

## The check — `page-fetch-worker-only`

`.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/page-fetch-worker-only.mjs`, blocking, registered in `pack.mjs`. Three finding kinds:

1. an importer of the surface that sits **outside any task directory**;
2. an importing task whose `task.mjs` declares **no `agent_preprocessing`** worker;
3. an importing task whose `task.mjs` **omits `SCRAPER_API_KEY`** from `required_secrets` — the finding points at the `task.mjs` (the file to edit), not the importer, and fires once per task however many workers import.

Design notes:

- **The owning task is found by its declaration, not a hardcoded pack path** — the nearest ancestor directory holding a `task.mjs`, probed with `ctx.exists` so a `--changed` run still resolves it. The check survives the pack (or its `tasks/` tree) being moved.
- **Parsing beats grepping, twice.** Import/require *specifiers* are matched structurally, so a comment citing `scraperapi.mjs` by name (`prepare.mjs` has one) is documentation, not use. And `required_secrets` / `agent_preprocessing` are matched only as real keys at a line start, so `create-extractor`'s five-line comment *about* `required_secrets` — or a commented-out declaration — can never answer for the declaration itself.
- **Tests are exempt**: the surface's own test imports it to exercise the URL builder and never fetches, so a `test/` file neither needs a secret nor implies its task does.
- **Scope stated honestly in the header**: this catches use of the *declared* surface. A hand-rolled `fetch()` of an event page straight to some other vendor is not statically detectable (a page URL looks like any other URL) and stays the reader's job.
